title: Introduce policy-telemetry adapter and CMK handoff audit sealing
author: Marisol Chen
description: Background and motivation: We need richer telemetry for RBACv2 policy decisions so security teams can correlate decision signals with CMK (customer-managed key) usage and data-residency enforcement while preserving an immutable audit trail. This change adds a lightweight policy-telemetry adapter that emits per-decision metadata to the audit sealer and wires a CMK handoff flow that records proof-of-handoff for cross-region key delegations. Goals: (1) capture policy input vectors and scoring metadata for RBACv2 decisions, (2) stamp audit envelopes with CMK provenance when a delegated key is used or handed off, (3) keep latency impact sub-5ms on hot paths and run in shadow mode by default for the initial rollout. What this PR does (high level): - New adapter service: src/server/policy_telemetry/adapter.go and internal protobufs for a compact per-decision telemetry payload. The adapter lives behind the policy engine and exports a non-blocking gRPC/HTTP endpoint that the audit sealer can consume. - Audit sealer integration: pkg/audit/sealer/service.go updated to accept TelemetryEnvelope objects and include a CMK-proof section when the CMK handoff occurs. - CMK handoff protocol: small state machine added to pkg/crypto/cmk_handoff.go to produce a signed CMK-handshake ticket that is stored alongside the audit envelope (sealed by our root-key and including the original request's residency hint). - DB migration: migrations/20260210_add_policy_telemetry_table.sql introduces telemetry_store for long-term sampling and bloom-index keys for fast lookup. - RBAC rules: rules/policy_templates/added_labels.yaml adds optional scoring labels that the policy engine can populate; this is backward compatible and ignored when the adapter is disabled. - Ops and deployment: deploy/privileged-role.yaml grants the sealer the minimum KMS wrap/unwrap permission; deploy/helm/values.yaml includes a feature flag policyTelemetry.enabled defaulting to false. - Tests and CI: tests/integration/test_policy_telemetry.py and tests/e2e/test_cmk_handoff_flow.sh simulate cross-region handoffs in the integration environment. Rollout plan: default is shadow mode (telemetry recorded but not used in auth decisions). After 2 weeks of sampling and a brief regression window with quality gates, we'll flip the runtime flag and enable per-route enforcement for a small set of internal operator teams. Backwards compatibility: adapter is optional; when disabled the sealer continues to write audit envelopes without telemetry sections. Security review notes: CMK handshake ticket is signed with our internal attestation key and includes a nonce + residency claim; no plaintext key material is written to telemetry_store. Migration path: a write-only collector is safe for first deploy. See docs/security/policy-telemetry.md for operational runbook and sampling guidance.

review_thread: Avi Patel (2026-02-16): Can the adapter operate in-process to avoid RPC overhead? Concern: extra hop on hot policy path.

Marisol Chen (2026-02-16): We measured the in-process approach in a prototype; separating via non-blocking gRPC gives better isolation and allows independent scaling. We added micro-batching to keep p99 impact <5ms.
Gabrielle Ortiz (2026-02-17): Please ensure the CMK handshake ticket contains no key material and is forward portable for third-party auditors. Add field-level docs to telemetry.proto.
Marisol Chen (2026-02-17): Updated telemetry.proto with explicit provenance fields and a non-exportable key-id reference. Confirmed no plaintext keys are stored.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-18): Tests pass but noticed the sealer might retry KMS unwrap synchronously. We should offload retry/backoff to the async worker to avoid blocking envelope writes.
Marisol Chen (2026-02-18): Moved KMS retry into the worker queue and added circuit-breaker metrics; added integration test for transient KMS failures.
Avi Patel (2026-02-19): Approved after minor nits; please add release-note summarizing operations impact.
Gabrielle Ortiz (2026-02-20): Security review complete; LGTM.

merge_outcome: Merged via squash on main. Release gating: feature flag policyTelemetry.enabled=false by default. Ops: must update KMS role in prod before enabling in a region.
release_notes: Add optional policy-telemetry adapter and CMK handoff audit sealing. Defaulted to shadow mode; no behavior change for existing tenants until policyTelemetry.enabled=true. Operators must provision new minimal KMS wrap/unwrap role before enabling. Includes DB migration to add telemetry_store (write-only by default).
security_impact: Improves forensic capability for RBACv2 decisions and provides auditable CMK handoff proofs. No secret materials are written to telemetry storage. Access to telemetry_store requires audit-logged roles; deploys gated by security review.
